hero.label: Made for Alex
hero.headline: I want to sell the AI recruiter that makes my job obsolete.
hero.subheadline: Alex is automating the most time-consuming parts of recruiting, and the market is just now catching up to what agentic AI can actually do. I spent over a year as a BDR doing exactly what Alex sells against: manual outreach, repetitive screening, clunky scheduling. I want to be on the side that fixes it.

whyCompany.title: Alex is solving a problem every hiring team feels daily
whyCompany.body: Sourcing, screening, and scheduling are the three tasks recruiters lose the most time to, and Alex puts all three on autopilot. That is not a feature, that is a category. Selling a product that removes real pain from a buyer's week is the easiest conversation to start.

whyCompany.title: A $17M raise and YC traction means the pipeline is ready to scale
whyCompany.body: Alex raised $17M and is one of the fastest-growing companies out of its YC batch, which means the proof points exist but the outbound motion is still being built. This is exactly the moment an SDR can have outsized impact, before the playbook is set and while there is still room to shape it.

whyCompany.title: I have already done this job, just without the AI product behind me
whyCompany.body: At Copygen.ai I ran cold outreach sequences in HubSpot, built LinkedIn cadences, and helped close 15 to 20 paying clients from scratch with no brand name behind me. At NextAfter I learned how B2B buyers think and how to develop messaging that converts. Selling Alex means combining both skill sets with a product that actually sells itself.

quote: I spent a year manually doing what Alex automates. I know exactly where recruiters feel the pain, and I know how to have that conversation in a way that makes them want to see a demo the same day.
